solution: Add the daily rates: \(\frac{1}{30} + \frac{1}{40} = \frac{4 + 3}{120} = \frac{7}{120}\) of the work per day. Together they need \(\frac{120}{7} \approx 17.14\) days.
Add the daily rates: \(\frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{18} = \frac{3 + 2}{36} = \frac{5}{36}\) of the work per day. Together they take \(\frac{36}{5} = 7.2\) days.
B's daily rate is the joint rate minus A's: \(\frac{1}{20} - \frac{1}{30} = \frac{3 - 2}{60} = \frac{1}{60}\). So B alone finishes the work in 60 days.

value: 19 days in total (A: 3 days, B: 16 days)
note: total time asked, not B's share; checked: 3/15 + 16/20 = 1
solution: In 3 days A does \(\frac{3}{15} = \frac{1}{5}\) of the work, leaving \(\frac{4}{5}\). B alone needs \(\frac{4}{5} \times 20 = 16\) days for it. The work is finished in \(3 + 16 = 19\) days.
A quarter of the work takes 10 days, so the whole work takes \(4 \times 10 = 40\) days.

note: checked: A's rate 1/10 = 2 x B's rate 1/20
solution: Time is inversely proportional to efficiency. A works twice as fast as B, so A needs half of B's time: \(\frac{20}{2} = 10\) days.
Add the daily rates: \(\frac{1}{8} + \frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{24} = \frac{3 + 2 + 1}{24} = \frac{1}{4}\) of the work per day. Together they finish it in 4 days.
If B takes \(t\) days, A takes \(2t\) days, so \(\frac{1}{t} + \frac{1}{2t} = \frac{3}{2t} = \frac{1}{12}\). This gives \(2t = 36\), so \(t = 18\). B alone takes 18 days.

note: checked: A=1/24, B=1/40, C=1/60 give all three pair rates
solution: Adding the three pair rates counts each person twice: \(\frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{15} = \frac{6 + 5 + 4}{60} = \frac{1}{4}\), so A, B and C together do \(\frac{1}{8}\) per day. A's rate is \(\frac{1}{8} - \frac{1}{12} = \frac{1}{24}\). A alone takes 24 days.
The work needs \(10 \times 15 = 150\) man-days. With 6 men it takes \(\frac{150}{6} = 25\) days.
The boy's daily rate is \(\frac{1}{12} - \frac{1}{18} = \frac{3 - 2}{36} = \frac{1}{36}\). So the boy alone completes the work in 36 days.
Time is inversely proportional to efficiency. At full efficiency he works \(\frac{3}{2}\) times as fast, so he needs \(18 \times \frac{2}{3} = 12\) days.
If \(40\%\) of the work takes 10 days, \(100\%\) takes \(10 \times \frac{100}{40} = 25\) days.
B's daily rate is \(\frac{1}{15} - \frac{1}{20} = \frac{4 - 3}{60} = \frac{1}{60}\). So B alone finishes the work in 60 days.
A's daily rate is \(\frac{1}{10} - \frac{1}{20} = \frac{1}{20}\). So A alone does the work in 20 days.

Let a man do \(m\) and a boy \(b\) of the work per day: \(3m + 4b = \frac{1}{12}\) and \(4m + 3b = \frac{1}{10}\). Adding gives \(m + b = \frac{11}{420}\) and subtracting gives \(m - b = \frac{7}{420}\), so \(m = \frac{9}{420}\) and \(b = \frac{2}{420}\). Then \(2m + 3b = \frac{24}{420} = \frac{2}{35}\), so the work takes \(\frac{35}{2} = 17.5\) days.
Time is inversely proportional to efficiency. At normal efficiency he is \(\frac{4}{5}\) as fast, so he needs \(8 \times \frac{5}{4} = 10\) days.
C's daily rate is \(\frac{1}{6} - \frac{1}{9} = \frac{3 - 2}{18} = \frac{1}{18}\). So C alone completes the work in 18 days.
If Ravi takes \(t\) days, Ajay takes \(2t\) days, so \(\frac{1}{t} + \frac{1}{2t} = \frac{3}{2t} = \frac{1}{12}\). This gives \(t = 18\). Ravi alone takes 18 days.
A third of the work takes 5 days, so the full work takes \(3 \times 5 = 15\) days.

note: checked: 5 x 8 x 40 = 1600 = 8 x 10 x 20 man-hours
solution: The work needs \(8 \times 10 \times 20 = 1600\) man-hours. Five men working 8 hours a day put in 40 man-hours a day, so they need \(\frac{1600}{40} = 40\) days.

Each 2-day pair does \(\frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{15} = \frac{1}{6}\) of the job, so 5 pairs (10 days) finish \(\frac{5}{6}\). On day 11 A does \(\frac{1}{10}\), leaving \(\frac{1}{6} - \frac{1}{10} = \frac{1}{15}\). B finishes exactly that on day 12, so the job takes 12 days.
If Manoj takes \(t\) days, Anjali takes \(\frac{t}{2}\) and Amit \(\frac{t}{3}\). Their rates add to \(\frac{1}{t} + \frac{2}{t} + \frac{3}{t} = \frac{6}{t} = 1\). So Manoj takes 6 days.

value: 10 days (a man and a woman each do 1/100 per day)
solution: Both groups finish in 10 days, so \(4m + 6w = 3m + 7w\), which gives \(m = w\). Then \(10w = \frac{1}{10}\), so each person does \(\frac{1}{100}\) per day. Five men and five women do \(\frac{10}{100} = \frac{1}{10}\) per day, so they need 10 days.
B works at \(160\%\) of A's rate, so B needs \(\frac{100}{160}\) of A's time: \(24 \times \frac{100}{160} = 15\) days.
B's one-day work is the joint rate minus A's rate: \(\frac{1}{12} - \frac{1}{20} = \frac{5 - 3}{60} = \frac{1}{30}\). So B alone completes the work in 30 days.

If \(\frac{5}{8}\) of the work takes 10 days, the whole work takes \(10 \times \frac{8}{5} = 16\) days. The remaining \(\frac{3}{8}\) takes \(\frac{3}{8} \times 16 = 6\) days, so he needs 6 more days.
The work needs \(6 \times 9 = 54\) man-days. With 18 men it takes \(\frac{54}{18} = 3\) days.

note: checked: rate ratio 3:2, so time ratio 2:3, 20:30
solution: Being \(50\%\) more efficient, A works at \(1.5\) times B's rate, so A needs \(\frac{1}{1.5}\) of B's time. A takes \(\frac{30}{1.5} = 20\) days.

Together they do \(\frac{1}{8} + \frac{1}{12} = \frac{5}{24}\) of the work per day. In 4 days they finish \(4 \times \frac{5}{24} = \frac{5}{6}\), so \(1 - \frac{5}{6} = \frac{1}{6}\) of the work remains.
Their combined one-day work is \(\frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{15} + \frac{1}{20} = \frac{6 + 4 + 3}{60} = \frac{13}{60}\). So together they need \(\frac{60}{13} \approx 4.6\) days.
B's one-day work is \(\frac{1}{9} - \frac{1}{15} = \frac{5 - 3}{45} = \frac{2}{45}\). So B does \(\frac{2}{45}\) of the work in one day.

note: checked: 12 days at full rate = 16 days at 3/4 rate
solution: Time varies inversely with efficiency. At full efficiency he needs \(16 \times \frac{3}{4} = 12\) days.
If \(\frac{1}{5}\) of the work takes 4 days, the whole work takes \(4 \times 5 = 20\) days.
Let A take \(t\) days, so B takes \(1.5t\) days. Then \(\frac{1}{t} + \frac{1}{1.5t} = \frac{5}{3t} = \frac{1}{24}\), giving \(t = 40\). So A alone takes 40 days.
If \(\frac{3}{5}\) of the job takes 6 days, the whole job takes \(6 \times \frac{5}{3} = 10\) days. The remaining \(\frac{2}{5}\) takes \(\frac{2}{5} \times 10 = 4\) days.

note: 6.48 is 240/37 truncated (6.49 rounded); checked pair sums
solution: Adding the three pair rates counts each person twice: \(2(A + B + C) = \frac{1}{8} + \frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{10} = \frac{15 + 10 + 12}{120} = \frac{37}{120}\). So \(A + B + C = \frac{37}{240}\) per day, and together they need \(\frac{240}{37} \approx 6.48\) days.
The wall needs \(5 \times 20 = 100\) worker-days. To finish in 10 days, \(\frac{100}{10} = 10\) workers are needed.
B works at \(1.5\) times A's rate, so B needs \(\frac{9}{1.5} = 6\) days to do the work.
B's one-day work is \(\frac{1}{15} - \frac{1}{24} = \frac{8 - 5}{120} = \frac{1}{40}\). So B alone takes 40 days.
6 men and 8 women are exactly twice the group of 3 men and 4 women, so they work at twice the rate. The work takes \(\frac{12}{2} = 6\) days.
C's one-day work is the three-person rate minus the A and B rate: \(\frac{1}{12} - \frac{1}{15} = \frac{5 - 4}{60} = \frac{1}{60}\). So C alone takes 60 days.
A is 3 times as fast, so A alone takes \(\frac{30}{3} = 10\) days. Together they do \(\frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{30} = \frac{4}{30}\) per day, so they need \(\frac{30}{4} = 7.5\) days.
If \(\frac{1}{3}\) of the job takes 10 days, the whole job takes 30 days. The remaining \(\frac{2}{3}\) takes \(\frac{2}{3} \times 30 = 20\) days.

value: A's rate exceeds C's by 1/30 of the work per day, so A is more efficient
solution: Subtract the two pair rates so that B cancels: \((A + B) - (B + C) = \frac{1}{10} - \frac{1}{15} = \frac{1}{30}\). Since \(A - C = \frac{1}{30} > 0\), A does more work per day than C, so A is more efficient than C.
Together they do \(\frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{15} = \frac{5 + 4}{60} = \frac{3}{20}\) per day. In 3 days they finish \(\frac{9}{20}\), so \(1 - \frac{9}{20} = \frac{11}{20}\) of the work remains.
The work needs \(12 \times 8 \times 15 = 1440\) man-hours. With 10 men for 18 days, each day must supply \(\frac{1440}{10 \times 18} = 8\) hours.

note: checked: 8 days do 20/24, day 9 A does 3/24, half of day 10
solution: A two-day cycle does \(\frac{1}{8} + \frac{1}{12} = \frac{5}{24}\) of the work, so 4 cycles (8 days) do \(\frac{20}{24}\), leaving \(\frac{4}{24}\). On day 9 A does \(\frac{3}{24}\), leaving \(\frac{1}{24}\), which B finishes in \(\frac{1}{24} \div \frac{1}{12} = \frac{1}{2}\) day. The work is completed in 9.5 days.
Let B's rate be \(b\), so A's is \(2b\) and together \(3b = \frac{1}{9}\), giving \(b = \frac{1}{27}\). A's rate is \(\frac{2}{27}\), so A alone takes \(\frac{27}{2} = 13.5\) days.
If \(\frac{2}{5}\) of the work takes 8 days, the whole work takes \(8 \times \frac{5}{2} = 20\) days.
